fixtures.label: Open-item floor — 4 columns, and the population rule
fixtures.description: The `open_item` FORMAT and the 4-column FLOOR. Its partner is `balance-forward-subtree`, which covers the other format. ⚠️ `format` is a stored POPULATION rule, not a template param, so the two states come from two captured DOCUMENTS and neither can be re-rendered from the other — and NOTHING mechanical enforces the pair: `lint:fixtures` check 5 only fires on declared boolean params, and check 4 is per-fixture parity, which one fixture and one golden satisfy. Neither is a near-duplicate; each is the only golden over half the template. Four jobs. (1) THE FLOOR — one account, no line carries a `reference`, and the running Balance column is absent by design on an open-item statement, so every conditional is off and the header is exactly Details / Date / Charges / Payments. The partner is the 7-column ceiling. (2) THE POPULATION RULE — `open_item` prints only invoices whose REPLAYED balance is non-zero and takes no date bound: `buildOrgStatement` refuses a `from_date`, and `to_date` defaults to UNBOUNDED so a post-dated invoice still shows. The narrowing cannot move the closing balance (a settled invoice contributes +total and −total to one sum). (3) THE PAYMENTS COLUMN IS NOT DEAD — invoice 2364 is partly settled, so a real settlement line lands in it. The column is UNCONDITIONAL (a blank cell reads as zero, not as missing data), so without a settled line here it would be frozen empty by every golden in the family. (4) A THREE-NODE CHAIN SCOPED AT THE LEAF — every line's frozen chain matches the scope, so the Account column correctly does NOT appear; the partner proves it appears when lines genuinely span accounts. Captured from prod org `Enemies Movie, LLC / (default) / Locations`, the smallest multi-invoice open-item account available (2363, 2371, 2364), at address `organization:YWRsfgi3ARPpivx4eLh7:open_item:-`. Re-captured 2026-09-09 on beta.386: `scope.name` is gone (core#92) and the heading composes from `organization_path`.

fixtures.label: Balance-forward ceiling — a negative opening, and reversals that are CHARGES
fixtures.description: The `balance_forward` FORMAT and the 7-column CEILING — Reference, Account and the running Balance all on at once. Its partner is `open-item-floor`. ⚠️ `format` is a stored POPULATION rule, not a param, so the two states come from two captured DOCUMENTS — and NOTHING mechanical enforces the pair (check 5 fires only on declared boolean params, check 4 is per-fixture parity), so this family passes every check with either one deleted. Neither is a near-duplicate. Five jobs. (1) A NEGATIVE OPENING — the balance forward is −$28,293.71 and the running column crosses ZERO on its way to $1,514.95. Nothing else here renders a signed money cell, and a dropped sign would be invisible on any all-positive document. (2) REVERSALS THAT ARE CHARGES — all nine settlements are `payment_reversal`, whose multiplier is −1, so `effect_cents` is POSITIVE and they land in Charges. The only fixture proving direction comes from `effect_cents` and never from `settlement_type`; a template carrying its own copy of `SETTLEMENT_CONTRACTS` would put every one on the wrong side. Expect, rather than repair, an empty Payments column down the page: a ledger side reading ZERO, not a dead column — `open-item-floor` carries the value. (3) THE ACCOUNT COLUMN — two sub-accounts, rendering what is BELOW the scope rather than each whole chain. ⚠️ Matched by UID, not by name. ⭐ Its old reason — `applyPii` masking one uid to two names across `organization_path[].name` and `lines[].organization_path[].name` — is FIXED (core#91) and the two now agree here. Match on the uid anyway: the uid is the identity, a label never was. The two rendered depths differ (one chain has a `derived` middle node) — correct, not drift. (4) THE REFERENCE COLUMN — three lines carry one. (5) A NULL BILLING ADDRESS, so the letterhead prints the name alone. From the widest prod org family (14 nodes), at address `organization-subtree:gql6Tjro2tSVrgP5NKOH:balance_forward:2026-08-01`. Re-captured 2026-09-09 on beta.386.

fixtures.label: The ordinary balance forward — a POSITIVE opening carried in
fixtures.description: The commonest shape of the `balance_forward` format, and the one neither sibling renders: a POSITIVE opening balance carried into the period. `balance-forward-subtree` opens NEGATIVE (−$28,293.71) and `open-item-floor` has no period and so no opening at all, so before this fixture the arithmetic a customer actually reads on a monthly statement — money owed at the start, activity, money owed at the end — was frozen by no golden. It is also a THIRD grid width: 5 columns (Details / Date / Charges / Payments / Balance). No line carries a `reference` and every line is on one account, so Reference and Account are both OFF while the running Balance is ON — a combination neither sibling can produce, since the 7-column sibling has all three on and the 4-column one has all three off. That matters because the conditionals are adjacent in the header and a mistake in one reads as a mistake in another. ⚠️ Do not delete any of the three as a near-duplicate: `format` is a stored POPULATION rule rather than a param, so nothing mechanical pairs them — `lint:fixtures` check 5 fires only on declared boolean params and check 4 is per-fixture parity, so this family passes every check with any two of the three removed. Each owns a state the others cannot express. Captured from a prod org with four unpaid August invoices and September activity, scoped from 2026-09-01 so the opening is the real August balance rather than a contrived one.
